01 / The challenge

What the job asks of your van.

Electricians compete on trust and responsiveness. Your van should look professional, show your registration body and tell people whether you do domestic, commercial or EV charger work. Whether you need electrician van signwriting, EV charger installer van livery or sparky van lettering, the layout has to work on your vehicle as it really is.

01

Lots of similar vans

Many electricians use the same white van and blue lightning bolt. Standing out takes a distinct colour or layout.

02

Domestic or commercial?

Customers want to know if you will take on their kind of job.

03

Registration marks

NICEIC, NAPIT and similar schemes have rules about how their logos are used.

02 / What to include

What your van must say.

  • Business name
  • Domestic, commercial or both
  • Registration scheme logo
  • Specialist work such as EV chargers or solar

Not sure what to include? Our guide to what to put on a work van walks you through it.

06 / Design tips

Build the layout around the job.

01

Avoid the obvious clichés

A lightning bolt can work, but a distinctive colour usually does more for recognition.

02

Use scheme logos correctly

Supply official NICEIC or NAPIT artwork and check the scheme’s usage rules.

03

Mention specialist services

EV charger installation and solar are worth a line of their own if you want that work.

Before you book

Electrician van graphics: your questions.

Can you include my NICEIC logo?

Yes. Send the official artwork from the scheme and we will follow their placement guidelines.

Will a dark van work with graphics?

Yes. Light or bright colours on a dark van give strong contrast. Grey and black vans suit this well.

Can I add EV charger installation?

Yes. Specialist services can have their own line or a small icon panel.
